name: Cathedral Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi
history: Santa Fe's first church, built in 1626, was destroyed in the Pueblo Revolt of 1680. An adobe parish church, La Parroquia, followed in 1714-1717. Archbishop Jean-Baptiste Lamy, a Frenchman, began the cathedral in 1869 with French architects and Italian stonemasons, building it around La Parroquia, then removing the old church. It was dedicated in 1887 and named a basilica on 4 October 2005, the feast of St. Francis.
arch: Romanesque Revival in yellow limestone quarried near Lamy, New Mexico, with round arches and Corinthian columns, a dramatic contrast to the adobe city around it.
features: The rose window and the Twelve Apostles windows came from Clermont-Ferrand in France.
La Conquistadora Chapel, in the north transept, is the oldest part, kept from La Parroquia.

look.d: Each tower was meant to carry a 160-foot steeple; money ran out. The north tower is one brick row taller.
In 2005 a round window with a dove was added, modelled on Bernini's window at St. Peter's.

fun: Willa Cather's novel Death Comes for the Archbishop fictionalizes the cathedral's origins.
journal: French stone in an adobe town. The towers stop where the money did, and it suits them.

quiz.q: Why do the towers have no steeples?
Which novel fictionalizes the cathedral's founding?

a: The oldest part, kept from the earlier church
